home.title: Fire behaves differently in space. NASA has the data. We make it usable.
home.lead: A control panel and a curated catalog of NASA PSI combustion experiments, read through a fire-safety lens — prevention, detection and suppression for crewed habitats, with a bridge back to Earth.
home.pillarCount: {count, plural, =0 {No investigations yet} one {# investigation} other {# investigations}}

pillarText.prevention: Ignition, flammability limits and how materials burn when there is no buoyancy.
pillarText.detection: Smoke and aerosols in microgravity, and what detectors need to see them.
pillarText.suppression: Putting flames out when the atmosphere itself is part of the problem.

home.curationInProgress: Curation is in progress: investigations appear here as the research team reviews them.
home.dualTitle: One body of research, two places to use it
home.lunarText: Lunar habitats are planned with an atmosphere different from Earth's, where materials can burn more readily. The catalog shows which PSI experiments speak to that — and where the data runs out.
home.earthText: Microgravity combustion research also informs smoke detection, suppression and protective equipment used on Earth.

about.title: About & data
about.lead: Space Firefighters was built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 (Flame in Freefall). It is not an official NASA product.
about.whatText: A catalog of NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) combustion investigations, each reviewed by our research team for what it means for fire safety in crewed habitats: prevention, detection and suppression. Every number in a record comes with its source; when a value is unknown it is shown as "not reported" rather than estimated.
about.statusText: Complete records have every vital field reviewed by a second curator. Partial records are identified and classified, but some fields are still missing — they carry a "partial" badge.

limits.partialGravity: There is no PSI data for partial gravity (Moon, Mars) yet; results bracket it between 0g and 1g.
limits.notModel: This is a guide to the evidence, not a flammability model. It does not replace testing or simulation.
limits.scope: Rocket propellant combustion is out of scope.

about.licenseText: PSI investigation records are published by NASA under CC0-1.0. Curated fields cite their own sources on each record.
about.guideText: The panel uses NASA GRC mini-book NP-2015-10-034-JSC (U.S. government public domain) for the prevention / detection / suppression structure, the page-35 findings, and the ventilation band on the flammability map. It is a 2015 snapshot: ACME, SoFIE and some cool-flame work appear as planned — PSI records say what actually flew. The assistant cites paraphrased passages with page numbers, not the full PDF.

dash.panelLead: Three categories NASA says are fundamentally different in space. Each one changes the chart; Explore uses the same filter.
dash.findingsHint: Myth → evidence → data. Each card points to the investigations that carry the finding.
dash.title: The smoke peak looks the same. The risk lives in the tail.
dash.lead: SAME (PSI-115) shows a ~7 μm mode in both 1g and 0g. What changes for detectors is the large-particle tail (d ≥ 20 μm): about 10× heavier in 0g at 8 cm/s.
dash.cite: NASA PSI-115 · DOI 10.60555/q0v5-1v28 · 8 cm/s PSD files

psd.title: Smoke size spectrum
psd.hint: Log diameter vs log PSD. The peak sits at the same size; 0g keeps a longer large-particle tail.

tail.title: Share of particles ≥ 20 μm
tail.hint: Same cutoff, two duct speeds. 0g is the taller bar in both cases.
tail.y: % of PSD mass with d ≥ 20 μm

atmo.title: Atmospheres NASA asks us to care about
atmo.hint: Sea-level cabin, planned lunar habitat, and suit. Higher O₂ at lower pressure makes materials easier to ignite than on Earth.

hardware.title: Four hardware families, not 26 isolated tests

items.items: Flame Design · CLD · BRE · E-FIELD · s-Flame · CFI-G

items.body: Detectors that separate smoke from dust — mines, submarines, buildings.
Up to 85% O₂ at the burner: closest envelope to a high-O₂ lunar cabin.
Cool flames and dilution (PSI-117 / 142) inform atmosphere-based extinction, not only water.

map.title: Flammability map (schematic)
map.hint: O₂ × flow speed, as in the guide’s Figure 8. We only plot sourced points; the ignite/extinguish curve is not in the tabular files.
map.caption: SAME points at 8 and 10 cm/s in cabin air ~21% O₂ (PSI-115 + p. 19). Band 0–30 cm/s: p. 21. Dangerous minimum near 10 cm/s: p. 31.

dash.suppressNote: The guide points to N₂ jets (BASS), inert diluents CO₂ / He / Xe (FLEX) and water mist (Mist → ISS in 2015). Tabular files here still lack time-to-extinction by agent.

gap.title: Honest gap
gap.body: There is no current PSI data for partial gravity (Moon / Mars) — only 0g and 1g bounds. Lunar habitat O₂ ≥ 30% at ≤ 10.2 psi is a design target, not a completed test matrix. The 2015 guide describes ACME, SoFIE and some cool-flame work as planned; PSI records say what flew. Fichas are still draft, so Explore may be empty; this panel reads the tabular files and the guide findings.
